title: Headless display server ignores --resolution and project window size, causing the root viewport to use 64×64
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduces in: v4.8.dev6.official [8898c2b3d] and v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]

The relevant code is unchanged on master as of 46173009dc (2026-09-25).


### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, Linux 7.0.0, GNOME on Wayland. Rendered runs used the X11 display server. Intel Core Ultra 7 165H.  The headless runs do not use the GPU.

### Issue description

With `--headless`, the main window has no size. `DisplayServer.window_get_size()` returns `(0, 0)` whatever is passed to `--resolution` and whatever the project's window size is. The root `Window` then falls back to the 64×64 minimum that `SceneTree` gives it, and that is what the scene is laid out in:

| Command                                          | `DisplayServer.window_get_size()` | Viewport visible rect, stretch disabled | Viewport visible rect, `canvas_items` + `expand` (base 1152×648) |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `godot --path . --resolution 540x960`            | (540, 960)                        | (540, 960)                              | (1152, 2048)                                                     |
| `godot --headless --path . --resolution 540x960` | **(0, 0)**                        | **(64, 64)**                            | **(1152, 1152)**                                                 |
| `godot --path . --resolution 960x540`            | (960, 540)                        | (960, 540)                              | (1152, 648)                                                      |
| `godot --headless --path . --resolution 960x540` | **(0, 0)**                        | **(64, 64)**                            | **(1152, 1152)**                                                 |
| `godot --path .` (no `--resolution`)             | (1152, 648)                       | (1152, 648)                             | (1152, 648)                                                      |
| `godot --headless --path .`                      | **(0, 0)**                        | **(64, 64)**                            | **(1152, 1152)**                                                 |

The second column is also what a full-rect `Control` gets as its size.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project, or create an empty project with a full-rect `Control` as the main scene and a script that prints `DisplayServer.window_get_size()`, `get_window().size` and `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` after one frame.
2. Run `godot --path . --resolution 540x960` and note the output.
3. Run `godot --headless --path . --resolution 540x960`.
4. The headless run reports a `(0, 0)` window and a `(64, 64)` viewport. The script then switches to `canvas_items` + `expand` at runtime, and the headless viewport becomes `(1152, 1152)` instead of `(1152, 2048)`.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[headless-resolution-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32676483/headless-resolution-mrp.zip)
